verbs.name: transcript.get
verbs.description: Word-level transcript of an asset: words with indices and ms timings. The indices are what cut_words addresses.
verbs.result: Transcript {asset, model, language?, words: [{idx, word, start_ms, end_ms, confidence?, speaker?}]} — `speaker` ('S1'..'Sn') is present on a word only after media.diarize has labeled this asset

verbs.name: transcript.timeline
verbs.description: EDL-AWARE transcript: every asset word mapped to its position ON THE TIMELINE through the current edit, so what you read matches what is actually on the timeline (not raw per-asset words, some already cut). Each entry = {clip_id, track, track_kind, asset, word_index, word, src_start_ms, src_end_ms, timeline_start_ms, timeline_end_ms}; a word reused across clips appears once PER clip. `clip` narrows to ONE clip (the SELECTED-CLIP view → feed word_index back into transcript.cut_words{clip} to trim just that clip); `track` narrows to one track; both omitted = the PROGRAM transcript (the output line in timeline order, linked video/audio de-duplicated to one entry per spoken word). The ONE shared word→timeline mapping the panel, cut_words, captions, and search all read. Read-only.

clip.description: Narrow to one clip id (the SELECTED-CLIP view)

verbs.result: {clip?, track?, word_count, entries: [{clip_id, track, track_kind, asset, word_index, word, src_start_ms, src_end_ms, timeline_start_ms, timeline_end_ms, speaker?}]} — timeline-ordered; `speaker` ('S1'..'Sn') is present on an entry only after media.diarize has labeled its asset

verbs.name: transcript.cut_words
verbs.description: Ripple-cut audio+video for a word index range [start_idx, end_idx] (inclusive). Cuts at word boundaries, NEVER inside a word — boundaries padded to word edges ±40ms. By default the span is cut everywhere the asset appears on the timeline (all clips). Pass `clip` (a clip id, e.g. from transcript.timeline) to scope the cut to THAT clip's timeline window AND its linked audio clip only — the SELECTED-CLIP workflow, so trimming a word in one reused clip does not also cut the asset's other clips.

word_range.description: [start_idx, end_idx] inclusive word indices from transcript.get

clip.description: Scope the cut to this clip's timeline window + its linked audio (the selected-clip view). Omit to cut everywhere the asset appears.

rationale.description: Why these words — shown verbatim in the review rail

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {removed_ms, word_range, text} — the cut span; one op appended

verbs.name: transcript.mute_words
verbs.description: NON-DESTRUCTIVE word mute — silence the padded source span of words [start_idx..=end_idx] wherever it is audible on the timeline WITHOUT cutting or rippling anything: the keep-the-timing sibling of transcript.cut_words (profanity/filler/name bleeps that must not change duration or AV sync). The span (±40ms word-edge padding, the cut_words tolerance) resolves to SOURCE time and lands as one edit.mute_range op per matching AUDIO-track clip (same asset, visible window intersects; clip scopes to one clip) — so the mute stays glued to those words through later trims/slips/splits. PLAN-THEN-APPLY: all targets validated before the first op commits (a bad target never leaves a partial mute); speed-ramped clips are reported in skipped[], never silently ignored. Each applied op is individually undoable (project.undo); unmute everything on a clip via edit.mute_range {clip, clear:true}. Word indices come from transcript.get / transcript.search / transcript.timeline.

asset.description: Asset id whose transcript addresses the words (media.transcribe first).

word_range.description: [start_idx, end_idx] INCLUSIVE word indices into the asset's transcript (same addressing as transcript.cut_words).

clip.description: SELECTED-CLIP scope: mute only in this clip (must be an audio-track clip of the asset that plays the span).

verbs.result: {muted: [{clip, range_ms}], skipped: [{clip, reason}], word_range, text, range_ms: <padded source span>} — NOT_FOUND when no audio-track clip plays the span (cut, video-only, or ramped), invalid_args on out-of-bounds word_range

verbs.name: transcript.ignore_words
verbs.description: NON-DESTRUCTIVE transcript ignore — mark source words [start_idx..=end_idx] as ignored for transcript-derived outputs WITHOUT cutting the timeline or muting audio. Captions and transcript.assemble skip ignored words by default; the source transcript remains intact so the UI can show ignored words quietly and project.undo can restore the ignore list. Use remove:true to unignore a selected word/range.

asset.description: Asset id whose transcript addresses the words (media.transcribe first).

word_range.description: [start_idx, end_idx] INCLUSIVE word indices into the asset's transcript.

remove.description: false/default = ignore the range; true = unignore/subtract this range from the stored ignores.

verbs.result: {asset, word_range, text, action:add|remove, changed, transcript_ignores:[{asset, word_range}]} — undoable via project.undo; invalid_args on out-of-bounds word_range

verbs.name: transcript.search
verbs.description: Find every occurrence of a word or phrase in the transcript, returning [start_idx,end_idx] word ranges (+ text + at_ms) — feed a match straight into transcript.cut_words or transcript.assemble. Word-sequence exact match after normalization (lowercase + strip surrounding punctuation, unless case_sensitive).

verbs.name: transcript.chapters
verbs.description: Auto-segment a transcribed video into TOPIC CHAPTERS (YouTube/podcast chapters) by deterministic TextTiling lexical cohesion — NO model. NON-MUTATING: returns the chapter list; feed each start_ms into edit.add_marker (one marker per chapter) or write them with export.chapters. Always returns ≥1 chapter for a non-empty transcript (the whole thing when no strong boundary is found); an un-transcribed/empty asset is the same INVALID_ARGS as assemble.repurpose.

max_chapters.description: Cap on the number of chapters (default 12, clamped 1..50). The deepest cohesion valleys win.

min_gap_ms.description: Minimum spacing between chapter starts, in ms (default 20000).

verbs.result: {asset, count, chapters:[{index, start_ms, end_ms, title, word_range:[lo,hi]}], next}

verbs.name: transcript.assemble
verbs.description: build a highlight reel from NON-CONTIGUOUS transcript spans. Each [lo,hi] word range maps to a padded source span; spans are placed SEQUENTIALLY in the given order (reordering allowed) on the target video track and mirrored onto the base audio track when the asset has audio. Additive at at_ms (default = end of the target track) so you can assemble onto a fresh track/project for a pure reel. One edit.insert op per span per track. SINGLE-SOURCE: pass `asset`+`word_ranges`. MULTI-SOURCE (stitch the output line from SEVERAL source clips/assets — the inverse of cut-from-each-source): pass `sources:[{asset, word_ranges}]`; spans are concatenated across sources in the given order.

asset.description: Single-source asset id (use with word_ranges). Omit when passing `sources`.

word_ranges.description: Ordered list of [start_idx,end_idx] inclusive word-index spans (from transcript.get) to keep — the reel plays them in this order.

sources.description: MULTI-SOURCE: ordered list of {asset, word_ranges} — spans from several clips/assets stitched onto the output line in order. Use INSTEAD of asset+word_ranges.

track.description: Target video track (default: first video track).

audio_track.description: Audio mirror track (default: first audio track). The reel's sound is placed here when the asset has audio — pass a track matched to `track` to avoid mixing into the base narration.

at_ms.description: Start position on the track (default: end of the target track = append).

pad_ms.description: Word-edge padding in ms (default 40 — cut outside the words).

rationale.description: Why these highlights — shown verbatim in the review rail.

verbs.result: {asset, sources, spans_placed, track, audio_mirrored, at_ms, total_ms} — one edit.insert op per span per track appended
